findings.highlight: Kiritsugu Emiya was one of the Masters in the last Holy Grail War. I fought alongside him for the Grail, and we won.
findings.evidenceJa: 前回の聖杯戦争のおり、衛宮切嗣はマスターの一人でした。私は彼と協力して聖杯戦争に挑み、最後まで勝ち残りました。
findings.governingReading: Saber says she cooperated with Kiritsugu and remained/won through to the final stage of the previous war.
findings.explanation: Saber and Kiritsugu surviving to the end becomes winning the war.

findings.highlight: As I push on the door, I don't feel particularly motivated to ask the priest about what happened ten years ago.
findings.evidenceJa: あの扉を押し開け、神父に十年前の出来事を尋ねる気概が生まれない。
findings.governingReading: Although he came at Saber's urging, Shirou cannot summon the spirit to push open the door and question Kirei about ten years ago.
findings.explanation: Shirou lacking the nerve to open the church door becomes opening it.

findings.highlight: are firm and strong.
findings.evidenceJa: その動作だけで、筋肉という筋肉が硬直した。
findings.governingReading: The man's act of standing instantly makes Shirou's muscles lock. The following approach provokes an expectation of being killed.
findings.explanation: Shirou's muscles locking when the man stands becomes admiration of firm, strong movement. Shirou still freezes later as the hand approaches his neck.

findings.highlight: But then...why do I feel like I'm about to fight for my life?
findings.evidenceJa: それだけだというのに、何故—俺はこの男に、ここで殺されると覚悟したのか。
findings.governingReading: Despite the man's ordinary approach, Shirou inexplicably resigns himself to being killed there.
findings.explanation: Shirou accepting he will be killed becomes feeling he must fight for his life.

findings.highlight: I can't say he's wrong.
findings.evidenceJa: そう、それが当然だ。
findings.governingReading: The man moves away; Shirou thinks that distancing is the natural outcome and that his own death panic was abnormal.
findings.explanation: Shirou recognizing the man's withdrawal as normal becomes agreeing that the man is not wrong.

findings.highlight: "I don't intend to. I'm just here to ask you a question. Like I'd come just for the reasons you gave."
findings.evidenceJa: 「—そんな訳ないだろ。単に聞きたい事があるから来ただけだ。そうでもなけりゃ、頼まれたっておまえの所になんて来るもんか」
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he came solely with a question and otherwise would not come to Kirei's place even if someone begged him.
findings.explanation: Shirou saying he would not visit Kirei even if asked becomes rejecting Kirei's stated reasons.

findings.highlight: It's a repulsive smile, as if he's savoring the moment.
findings.evidenceJa: 密かな愉しみに酔うような、それは、不吉な笑みだった。
findings.governingReading: His curled mouth forms an ill-omened smile, as though secretly savoring pleasure.
findings.explanation: Kirei's ominous smile becomes repulsive.

findings.highlight: If Kiritsugu Emiya had given the Einzberns the Holy Grail, they would have taken him in as an official member of their family. Not unlike a noble family taking in a knight of unknown lineage and origins.
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を手に入れた暁には、衛宮切嗣は正式にアインツベルンの人間として迎えられた筈だ。何処の出とも判らない馬の骨を貴族に迎え入れるようなものでな。
findings.governingReading: 馬の骨 is a contemptuous nobody of unknown origin whom a noble house would admit.
findings.explanation: An unknown nobody becomes a knight of unknown lineage.

findings.highlight: In the previous war, Kiritsugu defeated many Masters. I was the only one who managed to survive battling him. The rest were almost certainly slain.
findings.evidenceJa: 前回の聖杯戦争において、切嗣は多くのマスターを倒した。ヤツと戦い、一命を取り留めた者は私一人だ。残りは確実に殺された。
findings.governingReading: Kirei states that everyone else who fought Kiritsugu was definitely killed; only Kirei survived.
findings.explanation: Certain killings become only almost certain.

findings.highlight: He was precise, meticulous, predatory, and ruthless. He had no mercy for his enemies. Once he decided to kill someone, they would die. He butchered Servants and allowed their Masters to beg for their lives only to pull the trigger once their backs were turned. He felt nothing after each kill. He felt neither pride in his own dominance nor guilt for the fallen."
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツは的確であり、周到であり、蛮勇であり、無情だった。敵にかける情けなどない。殺すと決めればただ殺した。サーヴァントを屠り、助けを請うマスターを這わせ、逃げようとする頭蓋に銃口を当てて引き金を引いた。殺した後の感慨もない。強さを誇る優越も、消えた弱者への罪悪もない」
findings.governingReading: 蛮勇 describes bold, rash or foolhardy courage within Kirei's four-part characterization of Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: Foolhardy courage becomes predation.

findings.highlight: He was precise, meticulous, predatory, and ruthless. He had no mercy for his enemies. Once he decided to kill someone, they would die. He butchered Servants and allowed their Masters to beg for their lives only to pull the trigger once their backs were turned. He felt nothing after each kill. He felt neither pride in his own dominance nor guilt for the fallen."
findings.evidenceJa: ヤツは的確であり、周到であり、蛮勇であり、無情だった。敵にかける情けなどない。殺すと決めればただ殺した。サーヴァントを屠り、助けを請うマスターを這わせ、逃げようとする頭蓋に銃口を当てて引き金を引いた。殺した後の感慨もない。強さを誇る優越も、消えた弱者への罪悪もない」
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu made pleading Masters crawl, then put a gun to the skulls of those trying to flee and pulled the trigger.
findings.explanation: Crawling fugitives become petitioners shot after turning their backs.

findings.highlight: "Let me put it another way. If Kiritsugu was part of this war, he would be the worst possible Master for you to face. If you consider ruthlessness a form of evil, then he would have been the most obvious source of evil in the last war. He had nothing else, after all."
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうだな。もし今回の戦いに切嗣がいるのなら、おまえが最も嫌悪するマスターになっただろう。非情だという事が悪になるのなら、前回の戦いで最も判りやすい悪は、あの男をおいて他にはなかったのだから」
findings.governingReading: If ruthlessness constitutes evil, Kirei says no one in the previous war was a more obvious evil than Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: A causal explanation is invented after Kirei calls Kiritsugu the clearest evil.

findings.highlight: One so easily changed by magical suggestion or merely hardening their heart would not have been worthy of obtaining the grail. That must have been his belief. So he adopted the identity of a killer through and through.
findings.evidenceJa: “冷徹である”という異なる人格さえ用意すれば容易いものを、そんな人間では聖杯に届かない、届く価値がないと信じたのだろう」
findings.governingReading: Kirei says Kiritsugu could easily have prepared a separate 'cold-blooded' personality, but likely believed such a person could neither reach nor deserve the Grail.
findings.explanation: Refusing a separate killer persona becomes adopting one.

findings.highlight: "He cast all of them aside on that altar.
findings.evidenceJa: 「その全てを、ヤツは土壇場で切り捨てた。
findings.governingReading: 土壇場で means at the last moment or in the final crunch: Kiritsugu discarded everything at the decisive end.
findings.explanation: The final critical moment becomes an altar.

findings.highlight: But, the one thing that I do know for certain is...
findings.evidenceJa: ……判るのは今の話に何一つ嘘がなかった事と—
findings.governingReading: What Shirou can tell is that nothing in Kirei's account was a lie, and that the otherwise indifferent man bears anger toward Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: Shirou's certainty that none of the account was false disappears.

findings.highlight: "Naturally. We stood at opposite extremes. We were born to be each other's nemeses. You might compare us to the Makiris and the Einzberns, but we both understood each other as natural enemies."
findings.evidenceJa: 「当然だ。ヤツと私は両極に位置していた。私とあの男は生まれついての仇敵だ。マキリやアインツベルンには同類として映ったらしいが、私たちは共に、互いを天敵だと認識していた」
findings.governingReading: Makiri and Einzbern apparently regarded Kirei and Kiritsugu as the same kind, although the two saw each other as natural enemies.
findings.explanation: The old families' comparison becomes Kirei's comparison of families.

findings.highlight: "...And you're different? He was someone who avoided getting hurt. While you say you were hurt, as you took a path embracing humanity. Being a priest made you different from Kiritsugu...?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「……じゃあ、アンタは違うのか。傷を負わないのでもなく、傷しかないのでもない。斬られれば傷を負う、まっとうな人間だって。アンタは神父だから、そこが切嗣とは違うと……？」
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether Kirei is different: neither one who suffers no wounds nor one who has nothing but wounds, but an ordinary human who is wounded when cut; is priesthood the difference from Kiritsugu?
findings.explanation: Shirou's two extremes and ordinary wounded human become avoidance versus embracing humanity.

findings.highlight: The others viewed he and I as similar for other reasons.
findings.evidenceJa: 連中が私と衛宮切嗣を同視したのは別のところだ。
findings.governingReading: Others equated Kotomine with Kiritsugu on a different basis from the humanity Shirou has just described.
findings.explanation: The pronoun case is nonstandard, but Kotomine's comparison with Kiritsugu remains intact. This belongs in a language-editing discussion rather than this character dossier.

findings.highlight: "You've wished for something from an early age.
findings.evidenceJa: 「幼いままの願望を持つもの。
findings.governingReading: Kirei calls Shirou and Kiritsugu people who retain an immature or childlike wish.
findings.explanation: A childish wish becomes a wish held since childhood.

findings.highlight: The priest chuckles to himself.
findings.evidenceJa: 神父は声もなく笑う。
findings.governingReading: Kirei laughs without making a sound.
findings.explanation: A soundless laugh becomes a chuckle.

findings.highlight: "Such Heroic Spirits tend to be labeled as Anti-Heroes."
findings.evidenceJa: 「そういったものが反英雄と呼ばれる英霊だ。端的に言えば人柱や生贄がこれにあたる」
findings.governingReading: Kirei says, succinctly, that human pillars and sacrificial victims are examples of the Heroic Spirits called Anti-Heroes.
findings.explanation: The defining examples of human pillars and sacrifices disappear.

findings.highlight: ...It is, well, human to forget our own ugliness and substitute it with comedy or tragedy. With time, even reviled heroes are eventually treated as victims, and cease to be seen as pure evil."
findings.evidenceJa: ……まあ、自らの醜ささえ忘れ喜劇を悲劇にすり替えるのが人間だ。悪として葬られた英雄も、時が経てば被害者として扱われ純粋悪ではなくなってしまう」
findings.governingReading: Kirei says humans forget even their own ugliness and replace comedy with tragedy; over time an evil-buried hero is recast as a victim.
findings.explanation: Turning comedy into tragedy becomes substituting ugliness with either comedy or tragedy.

findings.highlight: ...They are something created by humans, and grow only thanks to human involvement. That contradiction is what exempts these enemies of the world from the corrective forces that would otherwise eliminate them."
findings.evidenceJa: ……人が生み出したモノでありながら、決して人の手が混ざらず成長するモノ。その矛盾こそがあらゆる抑止の圧力を免除される“世界の敵”である」
findings.governingReading: The paradoxical being is created by humans yet grows without any human hand entering or shaping the process.
findings.explanation: Growth untouched by human hands becomes growth thanks only to human involvement.

findings.highlight: "...Of course, this does not apply to pure Anti-Heroes.
findings.evidenceJa: 「……もっとも、純粋な反英雄などそうはいない。
findings.governingReading: Kirei qualifies that there are scarcely any pure Anti-Heroes, then says such a thing does not exist and is only a human wish.
findings.explanation: The rarity of pure Anti-Heroes becomes an exception from the preceding account.

findings.highlight: "Well, unlike Kiritsugu, I could never do anything like will myself into changing for something I believe in. Though our objectives were different, so you can hardly compare us."
findings.evidenceJa: 「そうだ。私は衛宮切嗣のように、信じる物の為に意思を変える、などという事はできなかった。まあ目的が違うのだから比べるべくもないのだが」
findings.governingReading: Kirei says he could not, as Kiritsugu could, change his will or decision for the sake of what he believed.
findings.explanation: Changing one's decision for a belief becomes willing oneself into personal change.

findings.highlight: "You don't have to understand. Kiritsugu Emiya's wish was, in a word, 'peace.' Very simple, isn't it? So simple, in fact, that in a complex world it renders much unneeded. All he could do was dispose of or ignore all the excess and hypocrisy that didn't fit into his perfect ideal."
findings.evidenceJa: 「判らずともいい。ただ衛宮切嗣の願いは“平和”だった。実にシンプルだろう。シンプルすぎるが故に、複雑な世の中ではパーツが余ってしまう。その完璧な形に入りきれない余分は処分するしかない」
findings.governingReading: In Kiritsugu's too-simple design, the surplus parts that do not fit its perfect shape are sacrifices; the text overlays disposing of them with ignoring them.
findings.explanation: Sacrifices to be ignored become excess and hypocrisy.

findings.highlight: He must have been so enraged in that moment.
findings.evidenceJa: ……ヤツに憤怒を覚えたといえば、まさしくあの瞬間だったろう。
findings.governingReading: Kirei says that if there was a moment when he felt fury toward Kiritsugu, it was precisely when Kiritsugu betrayed himself at the end.
findings.explanation: Kirei's fury becomes Kiritsugu's fury.

findings.highlight: The three founding families boast history and bloodlines the likes of which you and I can only dream of. Of them only the Tohsakas are natives of this land, but their grandmaster is the famed Schweinorg. If he is truly as capable as the stories say, then it is little wonder that their excellence has persisted in spite of mixed ancestry."
findings.evidenceJa: 始まりの御三家、私やおまえでは太刀打ちできぬ歴史と血筋を誇る者たちがそれだ。この中で土着の者は遠坂だけだが、遠坂とて大師父はかの時の翁だ。尤も、遠坂の大師父が伝え聞く通りの人物ならば、人種分けなど滑稽だが」
findings.governingReading: Kirei says racial classification would be ridiculous if the Tohsakas' grandmaster is as reported. The passage identifies a grandmaster relationship, not biological descent from him.
findings.explanation: Kirei's dismissal of racial classification becomes praise for excellence surviving mixed ancestry, adding an ancestry claim and reversing the force of his qualification.

findings.highlight: "...That said, the Einzberns originally conceived this Holy Grail. They have a thousand years of history. Few mage lineages have persisted for a millennium without fragmenting their bloodlines."
findings.evidenceJa: 「……といっても、もともとこの聖杯はアインツベルンが考案したものだ。彼の一族の歴史は一千年。分家も持たず、他と交わらずに一千の年月を重ねた家系は少ない」
findings.governingReading: Few lineages last a thousand years without creating branch houses and without mixing with outsiders.
findings.explanation: A millennium without branches or intermarriage becomes only an unfragmented bloodline.

findings.highlight: One thousand years. In the name of their quest, they have killed and killed and killed, committing atrocities beyond imagination, clinging to their inhuman madness since the Middle Ages.
findings.evidenceJa: 一千年だぞ？　聖地奪還という使命を盾に殺して殺して殺し尽くすなどという異次元の蛮行がまかり通った昔、中世より連綿と続いた、人の領域など逸脱した狂気の沙汰だ。
findings.governingReading: Kirei invokes the old age when atrocities could pass under the banner of reclaiming the Holy Land, then says Einzbern's unbroken medieval persistence exceeds the human domain.
findings.explanation: A comparison to a brutal historical age becomes Einzbern's own thousand-year killing campaign.

findings.highlight: "The Einzbern mages have gone beyond the realm of mere evil. Over the centuries, those monsters have never once strayed from their dogged pursuit of a shared goal that was forgotten only decades from its inception.
findings.evidenceJa: 「故にアインツベルンの魔術師は魔の領域さえ突破している。十年単位ですら忘却され消耗する集団の意思を、その何倍も繰り返したあげくただの一度も道を誤らなかった怪物ども。
findings.governingReading: Even a group's will is forgotten and worn away on a scale of ten years; Einzbern repeated that span many times without once straying.
findings.explanation: A collective will that normally fades within a decade becomes a goal forgotten decades after inception.

findings.highlight: And the sins of the father underpin your relationship with them."
findings.evidenceJa: おまえとアインツベルンは、そういう因縁の下にある」
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Einzbern stand under that inherited因縁: the charged connection produced by Kiritsugu's betrayal.
findings.explanation: A historically inherited tie becomes the sins of the father.

findings.highlight: "You seem to understand. While all Masters have some connection to this matter, the obsession of the Makiris and Einzberns cannot be described in mere words. The Makiris have chased it for five hundred years; the Einzberns, a thousand.
findings.evidenceJa: 「理解したかな。マスターになる者は皆何らかの業を背負っているが、中でもマキリとアインツベルンの執念は言葉に表せるものではない。マキリが五百年ならば、アインツベルンは一千年だ。
findings.governingReading: Every person who becomes a Master bears some kind of 業, a burden of karma or consequential guilt; Makiri and Einzbern obsession is beyond words.
findings.explanation: Masters bearing karmic burdens becomes merely having some connection.

findings.highlight: Not just anyone can obsess over a single goal for hundreds of years.
findings.evidenceJa: 何百年もの間続く執念なんて、それは人が対峙できるものではないからだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou has no words because an obsession lasting centuries is not something a human being can stand against or confront.
findings.explanation: Obsession no human can confront becomes obsession not just anyone can possess.

findings.highlight: "Don't look so downtrodden. Kiritsugu Emiya may have betrayed the Einzberns, but it was not out of malice.
findings.evidenceJa: 「そう落ち込むな。衛宮切嗣はアインツベルンを裏切ったが、それを非道となじる事はない。
findings.governingReading: Kirei says Kiritsugu betrayed Einzbern, but he will not denounce that act as inhumane.
findings.explanation: Kirei's refusal to condemn the betrayal becomes a claim that it lacked malice.

findings.highlight: "That is sufficient. If that is what drives you, then fight like your life depends on it. The longer it lasts, the more victims there will be. Do as Kiritsugu did and weigh lives on a balance, all to lure out your objective."
findings.evidenceJa: 「十分だ。それがおまえの戦う意義ならば、死を賭して戦うがいい。長引けばそれだけ犠牲者は出る。切嗣と同じよう、夜毎己が命を秤にかけて標的を誘き寄せろ」
findings.governingReading: Kirei tells Shirou, like Kiritsugu, to put his own life on the scales night after night and lure out his target.
findings.explanation: Risking Shirou's own life each night becomes weighing lives in general.

findings.highlight: The priest turns his back on me.
findings.evidenceJa: 神父に背を向ける。
findings.governingReading: Shirou turns his back on the priest as he concludes he has nothing left to ask.
findings.explanation: Shirou turning his back on Kirei becomes Kirei turning his back on Shirou.
